chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad and others, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, altogether from Ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Is'haq al-Sabi'i, from one who narrated to him, who said:
I heard the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) saying: 'O people! Know that the perfection of the religion is seeking knowledge and acting upon it.

Indeed, seeking knowledge is more obligatory upon you than seeking wealth. Wealth is apportioned and guaranteed for you; a Just One has apportioned it among you and guaranteed it and will fulfill it for you. But knowledge is treasured with its rightful possessors, and you have been commanded to seek it from them — so seek it.'

key_terms.أَهْلُهُ: Its rightful possessors — the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt as the legitimate custodians of religious knowledge
key_terms.الْعَمَلُ بِهِ: Acting upon knowledge — praxis as inseparable from learning
key_terms.كَمَالُ الدِّينِ: The perfection of the religion — the complete fulfillment of one's religious obligations
key_terms.مَقْسُومٌ مَضْمُونٌ: Apportioned and guaranteed — wealth is divinely pre-destined

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about seeking knowledge versus seeking wealth?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delivers a public sermon declaring that the perfection of Islam lies in two things: seeking religious knowledge and putting it into practice. He draws a compelling contrast — wealth is pre-ordained and guaranteed by God, requiring no active pursuit — while knowledge must be actively sought from its qualified custodians (the Imams and scholars). The sermon reflects the Shia theological emphasis on 'ilm as the core of religious life, and the imperative of seeking it from the Ahl al-Bayt, the 'rightful possessors' (ahl al-'ilm).

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, and someone else, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Is’haq Al Sabi’e, from the one who narrated it, said,
‘I heard Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘O you people! Know that the perfection of the Religion is the seeking of the knowledge and acting by it.

Indeed! And the seeking of the knowledge is more Obligatory upon you than the seeking of the wealth. The wealth is (already) apportioned, guaranteed for you all (already distributed). A just One<sup>azwj</sup> has Apportioned it between you all and He<sup>azwj</sup> and my<sup>asws</sup> sword Guarantee it for you all; however the knowledge is treasure stored with its rightful one<sup>asws</sup>, and you have been Commanded with seeking it from its rightful ones<sup>asws</sup>, therefore seek it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad and others have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa all from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Hamza from abu Ishaq al-Subay‘i from one who narrated to him who has said the following. “I heard Amir al-Mu’minin Ali (a.s.) say, ‘O people, you must know that religion becomes complete through seeking knowledge and acting accordingly.

You must know that seeking knowledge is much more urgent for you than seeking wealth. In wealth every one’s share is guaranteed. A just person has already divided the wealth among you. He and my sword guarantee you to receive your share.
Knowledge, however, is stored with those who possess it. You are commanded to seek knowledge from its sources (those who possess it). You must seek knowledge.’”
